directAnswer: Pope Adeodatus II was a Roman monk who reigned from 672 to 676. The Liber Pontificalis remembers him for his kindness to clergy and pilgrims and for restoring churches, and he refused to accept letters from Constantinople that reflected Monothelite teaching.

sections.h2: A Monk of St. Erasmus on the Caelian Hill
paras: Adeodatus was the son of a Roman named Jovinian and became a monk at the monastery of St. Erasmus on the Caelian Hill. Because of this, he is sometimes listed as a Benedictine, though the monastery's rule in this period is uncertain. As pope he enlarged St. Erasmus and granted it endowments. He is sometimes called simply Adeodatus, since his predecessor Adeodatus I is also known as Deusdedit.

The Liber Pontificalis praises his generosity: he increased the customary gift to the clergy and welcomed pilgrims and the poor warmly. He restored the church of St. Peter on the Via Portuensis and dedicated it anew. The same source records that he would not receive the synodical letters of the patriarch of Constantinople, since they still reflected Monothelite views, so relations between Rome and the imperial church remained cool.
He died on 17 June 676 and was buried in St. Peter's. Little else is known about his pontificate.

keyFacts: Born in Rome, son of Jovinian
Monk of the monastery of St. Erasmus on the Caelian Hill
Restored the church of St. Peter on the Via Portuensis

faqs.question: Why is Adeodatus II sometimes called just Adeodatus?
faqs.answer: His predecessor Adeodatus I is often called Deusdedit, so some lists count this pope as the only Adeodatus and omit the numeral.

faqs.question: Was Adeodatus II a Benedictine?
faqs.answer: He was a monk at St. Erasmus in Rome and is often counted as a Benedictine, but which rule that monastery followed in the seventh century is not certain.
